9.1.2 Finding Line of Reflection
When an object is reflected, the line of reflection is the perpendicular bisector of the
corresponding line segments joining each point of the original object and reflected image.
Let's observe the following object and its reflected image. Follow the steps to construct the
lineofreflection.

Step I: Join any vertex of triangle ABC to its corresponding vertex of the reflected image
DEF. Let's join B to E through a straight segment.
Step Il: Place the pointer of the compass at point B
Step Il: Open the compass with more than half of the measure of the line segment BE and
draw an arc on the top and bottom of BE.
Step IV: Similarly, using the.same opening of the compass, place the pointer of the
compass at point E and draw two arc on the top and bottom of BE which intersects
the previous arcs at point L and M respectively.
Step V: Join the point L and M by a line using a ruler.
LM is the perpendicular bisector of BE.
The perpendicular bisector LM to the line BE is the required line of reflection.
